title: feat(plugin-security): a declared membership key is staged per request, beside the registered resolver
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoJLr1A7TYy1k6cGE23eo9VQ)_
Part of #25234
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: semantic

PR 2 of 3 of ruling A on #25234 (ruling 6355640929, design 6344270438, landing plan 6370632236): the reader. `stageRlsMembership`, the one producer of `ExecutionContext.rlsMembership`, now stages the `ObjectSchema.membershipKeys` that PR 1 (#25513) declared, beside the registered `rls-membership-resolver`. It also closes the objectql registry `extend` door that PR 1's acceptance notes named. Liveness flips `planned` to `live`. PR 3 (the authoring rules) carries `Closes #25234`.

Serial against #25233 (PR #25515 also touches plugin-security): whichever lands second merges `main`. This head already merged `main` at `aa2dbab7`.

## What a declared key resolves to, and when

`current_user.KEY` = the distinct values of `valueField` (F) on the rows of the declaring roster object X whose `userField` (U) is the caller and on which `filter` holds, inside the caller's own Layer 0 wall for X.

- **Which keys, when** (`object-membership-keys.ts#stageDeclaredMembershipKeys`). From the policies about to compile, take the `current_user.*` names their `using` and `check` read. They are parsed once per predicate text by `@objectstack/formula`'s `parseCelToAst`, after the compiler's own `sqlPredicateToCel` bridge, and the parse is cached. A name the ObjectQL registry declares, and this request has not staged, is resolved. A key no policy reads is never resolved. The memo is per key on the execution context: a request that reads the key on `qa_po` and `qa_asn` issues one roster read (pinned).
- **Both compile sites** (`security-plugin-rls-filter.ts`). The read door stages just before Layer 1 compiles, with the `compilable` list. The write `check` stages with `withCheck`. A `using` and its `check` twin therefore read the same keys. The resolver half runs first and is unchanged (`stageResolverMembership`). It now records which keys it staged, so a collision can withdraw them.
- **The read** (`readDeclaredKey`): X where `U == userId`, AND the compiled `filter`, AND the caller's Layer 0 filter for X. It is projected to `id` and F and limited to 1,001 rows, under `{ isSystem: true }`, and Layer 1 is not consulted.

## Rider 1: Layer 0 system read, independent of audience and posture

- The read's context is `{ isSystem: true }` and nothing of the caller's. The middleware's total `isSystem` bypass means X's own row policies, which may read the very key this read feeds, are not consulted. A caller with no read on X still resolves its key.
- The wall is the caller's own. `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` over `tenantLayer0InputOf(...)` is computed with `isPlatformAdmin: false` whatever the caller holds, so no crossing applies, and a roster row in another organisation never counts. `tenantLayer0InputOf` is a new builder in `tenant-layer.ts`. It holds the input literal `computeLayeredRlsFilter` used to inline, comments included, and the read door now builds its input through it, so the two cannot diverge.
- The system context deliberately carries no `tenantId`. With one, the engine scoped the driver to the active organisation on its own, which would have narrowed a `group`-posture key below the wall. The `where` wall is therefore the only organisation scope, and the Layer 0 ablation below proves it is load-bearing.
- **Pins:**
  - Real engine: the portal set has no grant on `qa_supplier_contact`, and its own find of the roster is refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, while its PO read resolves the key.
  - Unit: four callers (`MEMBER`; `EXTERNAL` with `audience: 'external'`; `PLATFORM_ADMIN` holding `admin_full_access`; `TENANT_ADMIN`) produce byte-identical `find` arguments, asserted in full: the `where` with the org term, `fields`, the limit, and `context: { isSystem: true }`.
  - **Rider 2:** `MEMBER`, `audience: 'external'` and `TENANT_ADMIN` callers all read the same rows, so keys are not scoped to externals.

## Fail closed

| Case | Staged | Logged |
|:--|:--|:--|
| no roster row | `[]` (the compiler drops the policy, as for any empty set) | no |
| more than 1,000 rows, or more than 1,000 values after flattening | unstaged | warn |
| read throws; schema unreadable | unstaged | warn |
| `filter` refused by `RLSCompiler.compileFilter` against X's columns with no caller variables (non-lowering shape, a column X lacks, any `current_user.*`) | unstaged | warn, plus the compiler's own |
| tenant wall denies (no organization scope) | unstaged | warn |
| no signed-in user | unstaged | warn |
| a key two registry objects declare | unstaged | error, once per logger |
| a key the registered resolver owns (its `keys`, or one it staged this request) | unstaged; the resolver's value is withdrawn from the bag | error at boot (`SecurityPlugin.start`, naming the key and every declaring object) and once at request time |

A key already in the bag that the resolver did not put there was supplied with the context, and it is left as is, as the resolver leaves it.

## Explain (rider 3)

- **Object level.** The `rls` layer's `detail` gains one sentence per key this object's policies read. It names the key with its `label` and `description`, then X, F, U, the filter, and "resolved to N value(s)" or "did not resolve (REASON: detail)". It then says "Whoever can write 'X' can grant this key: holders of [...]". The holders are the security catalog's permission sets for which `PermissionEvaluator.checkObjectPermission` grants `insert` or `update` on X. An object whose policies read no key is explained byte-identically (control pinned).
- **Record level.** The `business_rls` rule reads `via: 'membership:KEY'`. The detail names the roster row that links the record ("the principal's 'qa_supplier_contact' row 'c_17' links them to 'S-1' (its 'supplier'), which this record's 'supplier' holds"). The row id comes from the staging read, which projects `id` beside F, so no second read is made. `ExplainDecision` gains no field (#24451's choice).
- Not changed: an empty membership set still reads `narrows` at object level (the existing composed-deny recognition), as for a resolver key.

## objectql: the `extend` door

`SchemaRegistry.registerObject` refuses an `ownership: 'extend'` contribution carrying `membershipKeys`. It answers `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 with the name `ExtensionMembershipKeysRefusedError`, beside the `defaultRowScope` refusal and before the contributor list opens. Measured first: `mergeObjectDefinitions` copies only `fields`, `validations`, `indexes`, `label`, `pluralLabel` and `description`, so the extender's key registered and was then dropped in silence. The new test is `registry-extension-membership-keys-refused.test.ts` (6). It covers three refused shapes, including an empty map; an owner with no key; and two controls (an extension without the key folds, and the owner re-registers).

## Liveness and spec wording

- `liveness/object.json`: `membershipKeys` and its 5 children are `live`, and `authorWarn` / `authorHint` are dropped in the same edit, as the row's note asked. The evidence is `stageRlsMembership`, `stageDeclaredMembershipKeys` and `readDeclaredKey`, with `membershipKeySource` as the second read point. `label` and `description` are live through `describeMembershipKeyDeclaration`, which is why explain names them.
- The `membershipKeys` describe and TSDoc and the `rls.zod.ts` "Where a membership key comes from" section and module note no longer say "not applied". The accept set is unchanged. `check:generated --fix` regenerated 4 reference pages and `state-counts/object.md`.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/25234-membership-keys-staged.md`: `minor` on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `patch` on `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/spec`.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-membership-keys.test.ts` has 21 tests on the real `SecurityPlugin` + `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`, `isolated` posture. In the fixture, `u_x`'s roster has S-1 active, S-3 inactive, and S-2 active but in organisation Y, so the key is `[S-1]`.

- Read door, insert `check`, and a CONTROL without the declaration (zero rows).
- Riders 1 and 2, as above.
- The memo (one read across two objects) and laziness (zero reads for a policy that reads no key). The key extraction covers dot, index and SQL-bridge spellings, a string literal, and kernel names.
- Fail-closed rows: no roster row, the bound (1,001 rows red, exactly 1,000 green), a `current_user` filter, a phantom-column filter, a key declared twice, and a resolver collision with the boot error. CONTROL: the resolver alone still supplies an undeclared key, with no error.
- Explain at object level (positive and both miss kinds), at record level, and a CONTROL.

**Ablations, each restored byte-identically from a saved copy:**

- Declared staging removed from `stageRlsMembership`: 12 red, 9 green.
- Write-side call reverted to `stageRlsMembership(context)`: only the insert-`check` test red.
- Roster read run under the caller's context instead of `isSystem`: 11 red, including both rider-1 pins.
- Layer 0 term dropped from the roster `where` (system context without `tenantId`): 8 red.
- objectql refusal disabled: 4 refusal tests red, 2 controls green.

**Suites on this head's code, through `os-verify-lock.sh`:**

- `@objectstack/plugin-security`: 219 files, 4594 passed, 45 skipped. `typecheck` (incl. the test layer) exit 0.
- `@objectstack/objectql`: 467 files, 8705 passed. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- `@objectstack/spec`: 792 files, 22953 passed, 1 todo.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 124 families. All 124 were run one at a time, with exit codes captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation on head `e35ae5da`: 124 derived, 124 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 unrun, all exit 0.

- One real finding, fixed in `e35ae5da`: `check:doc-authoring` refused the tracker id in three runtime log strings. The ids are gone from the strings.
- Four first-pass non-zero codes were environment, not findings. `check-engine-split-ratio` exited 2 on the shallow clone and passed after `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-18`. `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` exited 3 (no dist) and passed after a full workspace build.
- Those five were re-run on `e35ae5da`. The other 119 ran on `21cace53`, which differs from `e35ae5da` only by those three string literals.

## For the seat: the Tier H skills row, re-worded for `live`

The row from report 6370454361 says "planned: no server stages it yet". With this PR it should read:

> | `current_user.KEY` (a declared membership key) | the values of `valueField` on the rows of the roster object that declares `membershipKeys.KEY` whose `userField` is the caller and on which its `filter` holds, inside the caller's organization (for `IN`; read once per request even when the caller cannot read the roster; more than 1,000 values, a failed read, or a key a registered resolver also owns matches no rows) |
